metadata.description: A managed Kubernetes cluster with one or more node pools and a network. Derived from OSAC's `cluster` fulfillment type (osac-project/fulfillment-service); the spec is the vendor-neutral Intent contract a provider (e.g. OSAC Cluster Fulfillment via a fleet-manager hub + hosted control planes) realizes. Target Network.VirtualNetwork is registered; Platform.Hub is registered (ADR-043 relationship semantics).

instance_size.description: Provider-neutral size class (small|medium|large, ordered/comparable — common-elements §2.2, DCM ADR-014). Size by class IN PLACE OF cpu+memory; the provider maps it to concrete resources at naturalization (DCM ADR-023). anyOf enforces sizing by class OR raw.

count.description: Total virtual CPUs. The provider naturalizes this to its native cpu model (a KubeVirt domain cpu, a hypervisor platform's sockets*cores, a public cloud's vCPUs) at realization (DCM ADR-023).

sockets.description: Optional topology hint: sockets. Provider-support-dependent; ignored where not applicable.

cores_per_socket.description: Optional topology hint: cores per socket. Provider-support-dependent.

cpu.description: Unifies vcpu (VM) / cpu (BareMetal) / resources.cpu (Container) — the same concept under three names today. The provider naturalizes to its native model (kubevirt domain cpu, vSphere sockets×cores, EC2 vCPUs).

size.description: Memory allocation, e.g. 16GB or 16Gi (class-aligned quantity pattern — Compute Base Class `memory.size`).

hugepages.description: Optional huge-page backing (provider-support-dependent; validated against provider capability).

memory.description: Reconciles the drift the sweep found (VM had {hugepages,size}, BareMetal had {size}): `hugepages` becomes an optional Base element.

storage.description: The reference-discipline storage requirements descriptor (PVD-001, Compute Base Class shape) — numeric minima the realizing storage must meet. The requested performance class is the governed `storage_tier` element, not an inline enum here.

storage_tier.description: The requested storage performance class — a GOVERNED vocabulary (ADR-038 §2): canonical terms are `storage_tier` reference-data records (standard/performance/archive), each denoting a requirements floor. Name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036); profile decides bare string vs data_reference (ADR-007/ADR-039). Mirrors the Compute Base Class `storage_tier` element. Governed vocabulary `storage_tier` (ADR-038 §2); name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036). Profile decides bare-vs-reference.

guest_os.description: Guest operating system. Portable form is a reference to an os_image reference-data vocabulary (DCM ADR-012; layering §3.7) the target provider advertises via capability discovery (ADR-PROV-002); policy validates membership at request. Inline is the portability_breaking escape. Optional at the data layer (bare-instantiation philosophy): a VM may be declared by sizing alone; a profile MAY require it.

type.description: Inline OS identifier (e.g. linux-server-9). portability_breaking: a value with no os_image vocabulary entry — a review finding.

release.description: Platform release, e.g. 1.30 (a Kubernetes minor release) or a distribution's release stream.

host_type.description: The node shape this pool requests — the handle of a provider-advertised host shape (CPU/memory/disk class) resolved via capability discovery. A requirement descriptor the provider must satisfy, not a reference to a registered Resource Type.

instance_size.description: Provider-neutral node size class (small|medium|large) — sizes each node in the pool; the provider maps it to a concrete node shape at naturalization (common-elements §2.2, DCM ADR-014).

node_pools.description: Converted verbatim from the flat Compute.Cluster spec.

network.description: Converted verbatim from the flat Compute.Cluster spec.

api_url.description: Cluster API server URL once Realized.

relationships.description: Provisioned and managed by a hub (a fleet manager / hosted control planes): the hub has lifecycle authority — hosted control planes run inside it. For imported clusters use the depends_on (soft) edge instead. Unnamed per ADR-043.

Imported/adopted into a hub's fleet (OCM ManagedCluster semantics): managed, not contained — strength soft because an imported cluster survives hub loss (degrade-don't-break). Mutually exclusive with the contained_by hub edge per cluster-hub pair; unnamed per ADR-043 — the typed target is the context.

context.purpose: Declares a managed Kubernetes cluster — release, node pools, and network ranges — as one provisionable intent.
context.plain_description: The request for a whole container platform: which release, how many nodes of what shape in which pools, and what internal network ranges it uses. A provider (e.g. hosted control planes behind a management hub) turns this into a running cluster and publishes back the API URL, console URL, and admin access that everything deployed onto the cluster then uses. Namespaces, quotas, node pools, and workloads all hang off a cluster record.
use_when: You need to request a new Kubernetes cluster with a declared release and node shape rather than hand-building one.
You need cluster-scoped resources (namespaces, node pools, storage classes) to have a single parent record they cannot outlive.
not_for: A distributed storage cluster (Ceph and kin) — that is Storage.Cluster; this type is the container-orchestration platform.
A group of nodes inside an existing cluster — that is Platform.NodePool (this spec also carries inline node_pools; single ownership between the two is an open decision).
works_with: Platform.Namespace — the isolation boundaries carved inside the cluster.
Platform.NodePool — homogeneous slices of the cluster's node capacity.
Network.VirtualNetwork — the network the cluster is realized onto.
Compute.Container — the workloads scheduled onto the cluster.
Platform.Hub — the fleet manager above this cluster: contained_by when hub-provisioned/hosted, depends_on (soft) when imported; a cluster hosting a hub is just its contained_by target
